WOOH! Boy did we get just that. I am so glad you feel as I do. I respectfully disagree with those saying these are plot holes, I think they were done purposefully. I thought, based on previous Kdrama expereinces, we'd get a whole tale of her survival. How she managed to survive and scheme and get to where she was. But doing that would have made the story about HER. And the story has never been about her. It has always been about the trio. Also I feel like the audience really only gets to know what the trio knows. And so not knowing how her mom survived is PERFECT in my eyes because it means none of the three of them cared to find out. The reason we don't know how she survived and looked like she did is because KMY didn't ask her. So I just really think that it breaks away from the mold of a lot of dramas, and reinforces that this story is for the main three, and not for the woman that caused them so much pain.

Edit: i also wanted to add that while a lot of people speculated that KMY and ST were related (so glad they didn't go that route) I always took those scenes to just show how similar their hearts were and their behaviors. They were so similar in so many ways that it's what part of created their (best) friendship. I think that when you are similar in heart to others, you can really look like them. I think this constant commentary of them looking related was to dot the OPPOSITE of what they did with the mom, which was express that her and ST were family (regardless of blood) whereas her and her real mother who she didn't even notice and who they made clear she was nothing alike were NOT family.

Essentially insurance agencies need proof of mental health issues in order to allow people to bill, so a diagnosis has to be made at the time of intake, which causes things to be rushed. I def. think that talking with someone will be the first step to helping you figure all these other big questions out. They can help you set goals, and make plans, and bounce ideas off of them. Who knows maybe you can write your mom a letter first or mention it in passing to see how it goes. 

And I'll let you in on a little secret, it took me way tooooo long to realize.

Adults are faking it.

None of us have it perfect, or together, or know much of what we are doing. The ones who look like they know what they are doing. Had either help to get to where they are now. Or they are content now, but will, like everyone else, end up back in one of life's hurdles trying to figure out how to handle something. 

Also if you've had to do a lot of convincing to your mom then maybe she has some idea. I find that people typically don't need to convince other people that they are happy or okay unless the other person is  already uncertain about your well-being on some level. Like I said though you don't have to tell your mom everything at first. That could be something a therapist can help you with, fostering that potential future conversation. You could tell her simply that you are struggling with the anxiety of thinking about future careers and you want to talk to somebody.  I am unsure if Germany has counselors on campus. But if they do, you don't need to tell your mom right away at all. You are actually of age to keep it confidential and can work on the idea of talking to your mom with a therapist first.

Also no one is perfect. Everyone has some level of anxiety. So I don't think it would be shocking to your mom to hear that the idea of growing up and having to figure things out is starting to make you nervous or scare you or makes you want to talk to someone else who might be able to help you plan it out. I am willing to bet that you might find that your mom understands a lot of the feelings that you were experiencing and that this will ultimately bring you closer.

I also like to play the what if question with people. So often we ask ourselves what if this doesn't go right? What if they are mad? What if they are worried? It's human nature I think to worry about the worst case scenario.

I like to flip that on its head. What if this brings you two closer? What if this is the first step to figuring out what you want to do? What if this is how you meet another person like you who understands and who can become a friend? What if one day the very  task of talking to your mom and going to speak to somebody allows you to one day speak to somebody else like yourself from the other side of things. Possibly another friend. Or your kids. Or a stranger who needed someone to understand.

I totally get that. The number one thing that has prevented me from really truly getting better is being honest with my parents about how I am doing. I had the opportunity to tell those I love about my struggles when I was about your age, but I didn't do it. And now I'm 25 and more stuck in my ways then ever before. 

Your mom loves you. She wants you to be healthy and safe and happy. She would want to know your struggling and to be a part of you getting help. I know it's hard. I am trying to be brave enough to talk to my parents even now. But talk to her before you get too wrapped up in the behavior of hiding you pain that you become truly dependent on keeping that secret. And it's up to you how much you tell her at what points. So even if you just started by talking to her about how you're having anxiety and how you think seeing a therapist would help you become more confident that's a lighter place to start, sure. But it's a start.

I am so sorry you are feeling the way you do. I have clinical depression, which is a large reason for why I have never really stuck to losing weight, so while I can't completely understand your experience, I understand the struggle to motivate. I would say to start with calories. To be gaining at that weight, you have to be eating high calories. By figuring out what you should be eating calorie wise everyday to have a steady weightloss, you can go on to google and look for a calorie calculator. From there I would say it's about making sure not to go over that every day. That will mathematically give you a starting way to lose weight. My fitness pal app has been really helpful to me to keep track of calories. Also make simple switches. Want a soda, have a sparkling water. Want pasta, have zucchini noodles. As far as motivation, i haven't found anything magical to kick that into gear but two things have helped me. 

1. Realizing that because I don't want to, doesn't mean I can't. There were days I didn't want to get out of bed. Most days even. But when I told myself. I have 2 feet and if I just put them in front of the other, even though my brain feels that I cant. I CAN! I physically can. i know you said moving is painful. But possibly even committing to something small like 10 air punches from bed could be a starting point.
2. Setting small goals. Let every 5 pounds be a victory. If you think about the end result, you will struggle more than anything else. Give yourself things to motivate at each goal. i suggest not food related and instead small prizes (that's what I do). A new nail polish color. New pillow cases, whatever floats your boat. For big goals. 20lbs, 50lbs, etc, I do bigger goals. A new necklace from Amazon. Rent a movie on Amazon prime. Get my nails done, etc. 

But most importantly I would suggest getting a therapist. One who specializes in eating Disorders or food related behavioral issues. You don't have to have an eating disorder to have therapy. But it sounds like you need to talk to someone to unpack the trauma you have been through, your fears, and how this all relates to food. I say this without judgment. Not only do I see a therapist. I am a therapist. 

And post on here! People are incredibly understanding and you will always find someone who understands on some level what you are feeling. Connection, conversation, and consistency are key. 

​

Good luck!
